subject: Food Science
title: Canning Basics
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Canning Basics.

hook.text: Napoleon offered 12,000 francs to anyone who could preserve food for his army. In 1810, Nicolas Appert won with glass jars.

buildup.text: Canning seals food in airtight containers and heats it enough to kill all microbes that cause spoilage and disease.

discovery.text: Low-acid foods (pH above 4.6) need pressure canning at 121°C. High-acid foods can use boiling water at 100°C.

twist.text: Appert didn't know why his method worked—Pasteur wouldn't discover microbes for another 50 years. It worked anyway.

climax.text: Commercially canned food can last 5+ years. A can of corn from 1974 was opened and found nutritionally intact in 2019.

punchline.text: Seal it, heat it, shelf it. Canning fed armies and feeds billions.

quiz.question: Why do low-acid foods need pressure canning?
options: To reach 121°C—needed to kill botulism spores that survive at 100°C
